payload.summary: IMPL_REVIEW round 2 for gate-semantic-context-default-enablement at b74b3d2f. Multi-vendor review re-dispatched via review_dispatcher.py --mode alternative so reviewers had Bash and could build forged artifacts and run the gate themselves. Three of four succeeded: antigravity/gemini-3.6-flash-medium (69s, 2 findings), codex/gpt-5.5 (227s, 1), grok/grok-4.5 (291s, 1). pi failed again on OpenRouter HTTP 402 insufficient credits -- the same account condition as round 1, not a review failure. NOTE: the first dispatch attempt was lost entirely because the review prompt specified a finding envelope (severity/category/location/title) that checkpoint_findings._validate_finding rejects; it requires id/type/criticality/description/disposition and the dispatcher raises before writing anything, discarding all vendor stdout. Re-dispatched with the correct contract. This is the #286 family and cost one full dispatch cycle. OUTCOME not_converged on ONE blocking finding, and it is unanimous: claude, antigravity, codex and grok each independently constructed a hand-edited report that satisfies every gate condition while describing a measurement that did not happen. R1's fix closed the EMPTY body and left the PARTIAL body open -- report_describes_corpus re-derives the DENOMINATOR (counts, case ids, gate ids, consumer names) and nothing about OUTCOMES, so a document may account for the whole corpus and still contradict its own conclusion. The three other fixes verified real: R2's ScopeScoringError now routes through the shared ScoringError and all three scorers agree; R3's regenerated report carries a harness.fingerprint equal to HEAD's source digest; R4's four prose corrections are accurate. #337's fingerprint is genuinely usable -- path-independent, bytecode-independent, moves on a real scorer edit. No second decoration exists: the mutation suite carries explicit positive controls and test_every_condition_the_gate_declares_is_mutated forces each new condition to arrive with a mutant. The blocking finding is a MISSING condition, not an unproven one. All baselines reproduce exactly; worktree untracked set unchanged.

blocking_findings.description: The gate authorizes an enabled default from a report whose own body records failure. `verdict_pass` (_verdict_condition, :263-272) reads one top-level string, and `report_describes_corpus` (_describes_corpus_condition, :301-375) re-derives only the DENOMINATOR -- corpus counts, case ids, gate ids, consumer names. Nothing re-derives the OUTCOME, so a report can account for the whole declared corpus and still contradict its own conclusion. `__main__._check` (:188) has the identical weakness and is the other consumer of the same trust. REPRODUCED FOUR WAYS INDEPENDENTLY. (a) claude: a THREE-FIELD hand-edit of the committed docs/evaluation/semantic-context/report.json -- verdict fail->pass, delete fail_reasons, set index.indexed_revision to any reachable commit (a live run populates it anyway) -- makes the gate print NINE met conditions and exit 0, while the same file still records retrieval_quality and coding_context_utility verdict=fail with fail_reasons [unmeasured, index_tier_insufficient], 5 of 6 per_consumer entries verdict=fail, corpus.cases_scored 7 of cases_declared 19, and index.tier 'none' against two gates declaring min_index_tier 'live'. (b) codex, (c) grok and (d) antigravity each built the stronger variant: all 19 declared case ids present but every one scored: false, corpus.cases_scored 0, every gate and consumer forced to pass with fabricated measured/metrics maps -- schema-valid, and authorized. compose_verdict() guarantees pass <=> every declared case scored AND every declared gate passed AND every precondition held, so these documents are UNPRODUCIBLE by the emitter; they can only arise from a hand-edit or corruption, which is precisely the threat the module docstring (:44-56) says the second layer exists to catch -- 'the schema does not run on a file somebody edited by hand, and the gate does not run on a file nobody committed'. This is the same defect class as R1, incompletely closed. Codex's own round-1 resolution asked for 'every declared gate present AND PASSING and every declared case present AND SCORED'; only the 'present' half was implemented.
blocking_findings.resolution: Re-derive the composer's pass invariant onto the on-disk artifact, in one shared place that both _verdict_condition and __main__._check call. Every input is already in the report: (1) top-level pass => corpus.cases_scored == corpus.cases_declared and every declared case entry has scored true; (2) top-level pass => every `required` gate has verdict pass; (3) top-level pass => every per_consumer entry has verdict pass; (4) gate pass => index.tier satisfies that gate's min_index_tier. Mirror them as schema cross-field constraints in BOTH copies of context-eval-report.schema.json, matching this change's own stated two-layer doctrine (the schema does not run on a hand-edited file; the gate does not run on an uncommitted one). Add mutants for outcome contradiction: the existing content mutation sets (UNWRITABLE_BODIES, MISDESCRIBING_BODIES) only ever perturb corpus COVERAGE, never OUTCOME consistency, which is exactly why the suite is green on this hole.

non_blocking_findings.description: --harness-source and --harness-version together let a caller assert BOTH halves of harness identity, reintroducing on the new condition the exact property #337 was filed about. The #337 fix correctly closes the IMPLICIT case -- verified: the digest moves on a real scorer edit and the committed report matches HEAD -- but 03328270 added a second override flag alongside it. REPRODUCED: a report claiming version '9.9.9-never-installed' and a fingerprint of a MUTATED source tree correctly expires under CI's invocation (exit 3, both harness conditions unmet); adding --harness-source <mutated tree> --harness-version 9.9.9-never-installed yields exit 0 with 'the harness is still 9.9.9-never-installed' and 'the harness source still digests to 24ab...'. Non-blocking only because make/CI pass neither flag.
non_blocking_findings.resolution: evaluate() already takes harness_source as a keyword, so keep the injection seam there and drop both overrides from the production parser; the mutation tests can call evaluate() instead of main(). If the CLI seam must stay, gate it behind an explicit --allow-identity-override that the gate refuses whenever it would decide authorization.

non_blocking_findings.description: harness_fingerprint digests every file under src/context_eval/, not only source. Bytecode and __pycache__ are correctly excluded and the digest is path-independent (both verified), but a stray .DS_Store -- which macOS Finder creates on merely opening the directory -- or a coverage.xml changes harness identity. REPRODUCED by both reviewers: the digest moves from 0e24a910... to a different value, and the gate then reports harness_fingerprint_current unmet with 'the code that measured this has changed', sending an operator to re-run a full evaluation over a file with no bearing on behaviour. Cannot authorize anything false -- it only produces a false EXPIRY, and only when the default is enabled -- hence non-blocking.
non_blocking_findings.resolution: Restrict _source_files to source suffixes (or to git-tracked files), or exclude any path component beginning with '.'. Name the contributing paths in the failure detail so an operator can diagnose the cause instead of re-measuring.

non_blocking_findings.description: CONSISTENCY OBSERVATION, NOT A DEFECT -- probed for reachability and it held. arms.ArmError still subclasses ValueError while R2's fix established ScoringError as the one channel every scorer refusal reaches the composer through, and __main__._score_case catches only ProducerError/ApparatusError. PROBE: an inverted line span (end_line < start_line) injected into a recorded service response does NOT crash the run -- ri-12 rejects it upstream, the case is recorded unscored and the run wrote a report with apparatus_failure, exit 1. arms.top_k_files' k<1 path is unreachable because the corpus schema pins k minimum 1. Recorded only on the structural argument the R2 commit itself made: 'a scorer added later cannot be the one nobody remembered to list here'.
non_blocking_findings.resolution: Optional. Either make ArmError derive from ScoringError for the same structural reason ScopeScoringError now does, or state in arms.py why it deliberately does not.

orchestrator_questions_answered.question: 1. Did R1's fix close the hole, or move it? Partial-but-non-empty bodies.
orchestrator_questions_answered.answer: IT MOVED IT -- blocking finding 1, and the probe you named is exactly the one that lands. Empty and structurally-empty bodies are genuinely blocked at both layers (verified: 6 schema errors on the hollow report, 0 on a genuine pass). The residue is OUTCOME consistency, not COVERAGE. All four reviewers found it independently; the minimal version is a three-field edit of the committed report.

orchestrator_questions_answered.question: 2. Did the five fix commits introduce anything? Can report_describes_corpus make a legitimate report unauthorizable?
orchestrator_questions_answered.answer: NO on the unauthorizable-legitimate-report risk, YES on one introduction. The condition cannot wrongly reject: there is no case-filter or subset flag on the run CLI, so a partial-corpus report is unproducible, and any corpus change moves corpus.digest in lockstep -- a future corpus with a different consumer set EXPIRES the old report, which is correct, rather than being rejected while current. The one introduction is --harness-source (non-blocking finding 2). R2, R3 and R4 verified real and correct.

orchestrator_questions_answered.question: 3. Is harness_fingerprint_current stable enough to be usable?
orchestrator_questions_answered.answer: YES, with one qualification. Empirically: path-independent (a verbatim copy at another path digests identically), bytecode-independent (17 compiled .pyc files do not move it), moves on a real behavioural edit, and the committed report's fingerprint EQUALS HEAD's source digest -- so no operator is expired today. The qualification is non-blocking finding 3: incidental non-source files inside src/context_eval/ do move it.

orchestrator_questions_answered.question: 4. Is any check still decoration -- green on an unmodified tree AND never proven by mutation?
orchestrator_questions_answered.answer: NO -- I could not find a second one, and I looked. The mutation suite carries explicit positive controls (test_the_durability_predicate_rejects_the_requirement_it_replaced, test_an_unmodified_copy_of_the_harness_source_still_authorizes, test_the_authorizing_report_accounts_for_the_whole_corpus) and test_every_condition_the_gate_declares_is_mutated asserts mutated == set(CONDITIONS), which obliges every new condition to arrive with a mutant. Blocking finding 1 is a MISSING condition, not an unproven one -- a distinction that meta-test structurally cannot catch, which is worth noting in its own right. No vendor found a second decoration either.
